_description: Supplement timing rules, optimal dosing, and interaction constraints. Used by the Supplement Stack Manager to generate daily schedules and conflict alerts.

creatine_monohydrate.name: Creatine Monohydrate
creatine_monohydrate.notes: Timing does not matter for creatine. Consistency is key. Take daily even on rest days. Loading phase optional (20g/day for 5-7 days).

interactions.note: Insulin spike from carbs may enhance creatine uptake into muscle cells.
Some research suggests high caffeine may reduce creatine efficacy. Separate by 1+ hour if concerned.

vitamin_d3.name: Vitamin D3 (Cholecalciferol)
vitamin_d3.notes: Fat-soluble vitamin — must be taken with a meal containing dietary fat for absorption. Pair with K2 for calcium metabolism synergy. Test 25(OH)D levels every 6 months; target 40-60 ng/mL.

interactions.note: D3 increases calcium absorption; K2 directs calcium to bones instead of arteries. Always pair.
Magnesium is required to convert D3 to its active form. Deficiency impairs D3 utilization.

magnesium_glycinate.name: Magnesium Glycinate
magnesium_glycinate.notes: Glycinate form is highly bioavailable and least likely to cause GI distress. Promotes relaxation and sleep quality. Can also take divided doses (200mg AM + 200mg PM).

interactions.note: Calcium and magnesium compete for absorption. Separate by 2+ hours.
Magnesium can reduce iron absorption. Separate by 2+ hours.
Required cofactor for vitamin D metabolism.

omega3_fish_oil.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil (EPA/DHA)
omega3_fish_oil.notes: Take with largest meal for best absorption and to minimize fishy burps. Look for triglyceride form over ethyl ester. Store in fridge/freezer. Check for IFOS certification.

interactions.note: Omega-3s have mild anticoagulant effects. Consult physician if on warfarin, aspirin, or other anticoagulants.
Fat in fish oil aids D3 absorption. Good to take together.

zinc.name: Zinc (Picolinate or Bisglycinate)
zinc.notes: Take with food to avoid nausea. Zinc picolinate and bisglycinate have superior absorption vs zinc oxide. Long-term use (>8 weeks at 30mg+) should include copper supplementation.

interactions.note: Zinc and copper compete for absorption. If supplementing both, take at different meals.
Zinc and iron compete for absorption via DMT1 transporter. Take at different times.
High-dose calcium can reduce zinc absorption. Separate if possible.
Vitamin C may modestly improve zinc absorption.

vitamin_k2_mk7.name: Vitamin K2 (MK-7)
vitamin_k2_mk7.notes: Fat-soluble. MK-7 has longer half-life than MK-4, so once daily is sufficient. Critical companion to D3 for directing calcium to bones and teeth. Take with same fat-containing meal as D3.

interactions.note: Essential pair — D3 increases calcium absorption, K2 ensures proper calcium deposition in bones.
Vitamin K directly antagonizes warfarin. Contraindicated for patients on vitamin K antagonist anticoagulants.

ashwagandha.name: Ashwagandha (KSM-66)
ashwagandha.notes: Adaptogen for stress, cortisol reduction, and testosterone support. Can also take at bedtime for sleep. KSM-66 is the most clinically studied extract. Take with food to improve absorption.

interactions.note: Ashwagandha may increase thyroid hormone levels. Monitor TSH if on levothyroxine.
May potentiate sedative effects of benzodiazepines and sleep medications.
Both support stress reduction and sleep quality. Complementary mechanisms.

vitamin_c.name: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)
vitamin_c.notes: Water-soluble — excess is excreted, so split doses if taking >500mg. Enhances iron absorption significantly. Antioxidant support for immune function and collagen synthesis.

interactions.note: Vitamin C dramatically enhances non-heme iron absorption (up to 6x). Take together.
Vitamin C is a required cofactor for collagen synthesis. Take together.
High-dose vitamin C may reduce B12 absorption. Separate by 2+ hours if taking both at high doses.

vitamin_b_complex.name: Vitamin B Complex
vitamin_b_complex.notes: Take in the morning — B vitamins are energizing and can cause vivid dreams or insomnia if taken at night. B6 should not exceed 100mg/day long-term (risk of peripheral neuropathy). Look for methylated forms (methylfolate, methylcobalamin).

interactions.note: High-dose C may interfere with B12. Take B-complex in morning and C later if doses are high.
B6 enhances intracellular magnesium accumulation.

probiotics.name: Probiotics
probiotics.notes: Take first thing in the morning on an empty stomach, 30 minutes before food. Stomach acid is lowest before eating, improving survival of bacteria. Look for multi-strain formulas with Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium. Refrigerate if label requires.

interactions.note: If on antibiotics, take probiotics 2-3 hours after antibiotic dose to avoid killing beneficial bacteria.
Prebiotic fiber feeds probiotic bacteria. Take together or close together.

collagen_peptides.name: Collagen Peptides (Types I & III)
collagen_peptides.notes: Hydrolyzed collagen dissolves in hot or cold liquids. Can add to coffee, smoothies, or water. Take with vitamin C to support collagen synthesis. No specific timing requirement.

interactions.note: Vitamin C is an essential cofactor for collagen synthesis. Take together for maximum benefit.

iron.name: Iron (Ferrous Bisglycinate)
iron.notes: Best absorbed on an empty stomach. Ferrous bisglycinate (chelated) is gentler on the GI tract than ferrous sulfate. Only supplement if ferritin is low (<30 ng/mL for men). Recheck ferritin every 3-6 months. Excessive iron is dangerous — never supplement without lab confirmation.

interactions.note: Take with 200mg+ vitamin C to dramatically improve absorption (up to 6x).
Calcium significantly inhibits iron absorption. Separate by 2+ hours.
Iron and zinc compete for DMT1 transporter. Take at different meals.
Magnesium can inhibit iron absorption. Separate by 2+ hours.
Tannins and polyphenols in coffee/tea inhibit iron absorption by up to 60%. Separate by 1+ hour.

melatonin.name: Melatonin
melatonin.notes: Take 30-60 minutes before target sleep time. Start with lowest effective dose (0.5mg). Higher doses are not more effective and may cause grogginess. Not intended for long-term nightly use — use for circadian rhythm reset, jet lag, or occasional insomnia. Sublingual form acts faster.
melatonin.cycle: Use as needed, not daily long-term. 2-4 weeks max, then reassess.

interactions.note: Both support sleep via different mechanisms. Complementary.
May potentiate sedative effects. Use caution combining with sleep aids or alcohol.
Caffeine suppresses natural melatonin production. Avoid caffeine within 6 hours of bedtime.

l_theanine.name: L-Theanine
l_theanine.notes: Amino acid from green tea. Promotes calm focus without drowsiness. Stack with caffeine (1:2 ratio — 200mg theanine + 100mg caffeine) for focused energy. Can also take 200mg at bedtime for sleep onset support without next-day grogginess.

interactions.note: Classic nootropic stack. Theanine smooths caffeine jitters and enhances focus. 2:1 theanine:caffeine ratio.
Both promote GABA activity and relaxation. Good bedtime stack.

berberine.name: Berberine HCl
berberine.notes: Take with meals to reduce GI side effects and because it works by modulating post-meal glucose response. Mechanism overlaps with metformin (AMPK activation). Monitor fasting glucose and HbA1c. Can lower blood sugar — watch for hypoglycemia symptoms especially if combined with other glucose-lowering agents.
berberine.cycle: 8-12 weeks on, 4 weeks off. Long-term safety data is limited.

interactions.note: Similar mechanism of action. Combining may cause excessive blood sugar lowering. Consult physician.
Berberine inhibits CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, potentially increasing levels of many drugs.
Berberine can affect drug metabolism. Take 2+ hours apart from prescription medications.

morning_empty_stomach.description: First thing upon waking, 30 min before food

morning_with_breakfast.description: With first meal containing fat and protein

any_time.description: No specific timing requirement — consistency matters more
